{
  "class-be": "Close your eyes and let the music paint a picture in your mind, like a director framing a scene. Alors, imagine what the scene in the movie would be, Over.",
  "class-do": "Ecoute the note ringing at 440 Hz, the pure A that tunes our souls. Now hum or sing that pitch, feeling the ratio of vibration in your voice, Over.",
  "class-play": "Place your index finger on the second fret of the G string to sound a bright B. Start now, Over.",
  "class-milestone": "You have just conquered the perfect fifth, from C to G, resonating like a call across the hills. Voila! Bravo, Over.",
  "guitar-be": "Sit tall, inhale deeply through the nose, feeling the air fill your belly like a soft chord. Exhale slowly through the mouth, releasing tension, Over.",
  "guitar-do": "Ecoute the two notes back-to-back and listen for the distance between them, like footsteps on a path. Identify whether the interval is a second, third, or fourth, Over.",
  "guitar-play": "Place your ring finger on the third fret of the B string and your pinky on the fifth fret of the same string to form a minor third. Play the interval now, Over.",
  "workbook-be": "In your journal, describe the colors and emotions that the music evokes as if you were scoring a film. Let your imagination flow onto the page, Over.",
  "workbook-do": "Recall the exact pitch you heard and note how it felt in your chest, like a gentle vibration. Write down any images or memories that surfaced during the listening, Over.",
  "workbook-play": "Set up your recorder and capture a clean take of the interval you just practiced. Listen back with curiosity, noting where the sound shines, Over.",
  "workbook-reflection": "FHEAL: Feel, Hold, Embrace, Accept, Let go—allow any tension to dissolve like mist under morning sun. Offer yourself kindness, remembering that every note is a step forward, Over."
}
